If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. Do not invent slang or private shorthand for\nmathematical objects. The goal is prose that a third-party reader can understand\nwithout having read the agent conversation that produced the change.\n\n### Paper-gap notes\n\nFor the proof-gap terminology used to distinguish source theorems, internal\nproof obligations, and conditional helpers, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex`.  For documentation of discrepancies\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If Lean uses a Mathlib result or\nconstruction not present in the cited argument, explain that replacement\npedagogically before naming the formal declaration. If the cited assertion is\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\n\n## Proof Integrity\n\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\n\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\n\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\n\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\n\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\n\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\n\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\n\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. Ask: *Can a real proof be built on top\nof this?*\n\n### Warnings\n\nPlaceholder tactics (`exact?`, `apply?`, `library_search`) should be replaced\nwith concrete results. Debug artifacts (`dbg_trace`, `#check`, `#eval`,\n`#print`) should be removed from proof files. See the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference for\nthe full warning catalog.\n\n### Anti-patterns\n\nSubtler proof-evasion patterns that pass kernel-level checks yet still fail to\nprove the claimed mathematics are catalogued in `docs/anti_patterns.md`:\nconclusion-shaped hypotheses, definitional sleight-of-hand, zero-fallback\nbranches, trivial default witnesses, Mathlib-bypass castles, and external\n`*Statement` smuggles. Reviewers should consult this file alongside\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md`.\n\n## PR and Commit Conventions\n\nPRs are GitHub pull requests (opened by `local/bin/pr_open.py`, merged by\n`local/bin/pr_merge.py`); `#N` in PR bodies and commit messages is the GitHub\nissue number. Titles, bodies, and commit rules below are unchanged from the\nparent project.\n\n### PR title format\n\n```\ntype(scope): short description\n```\n\n| Type       | When to use                                      |\n|------------|--------------------------------------------------|\n| `feat`     | New definition, lemma, theorem, or module         |\n| `fix`      | Bug fix (broken proof, wrong identifier, etc.)    |\n| `refactor` | Restructuring without changing API surface        |\n| `docs`     | Documentation or blueprint changes only           |\n| `style`    | Formatting, naming, or docstring cleanup only     |\n| `ci`       | CI/CD workflow changes                            |\n| `chore`    | Dependency bumps, linting, toolchain updates      |\n\n**Scope** is a shortened module path: `LDT/SelfImprovement`, `Quantum`,\n`blueprint`, etc. Omit the `MIPStarRE/` prefix.\n\n### PR body template\n\nEvery PR body must contain three sections:\n\n```markdown\n### Motivation\n- Why this change is needed. Cite the issue and paper/blueprint location.\n\n### Description\n- State precisely what changed.\n\n### Testing\n- What was verified and how (e.g., `lake build`, `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\"`).\n\n---\nAddresses #N\n```\n\nUse `Addresses #N` (keeps the issue open) or `Closes #N` (auto-closes on merge).\n\n### Commit messages\n\n- **Imperative mood** in the subject line (\"Add\", not \"Added\")\n- Subject under 72 characters\n- When squash-merging, the commit message should match the PR title format\n\n## Review Process\n\nEvery PR touching Lean code is reviewed by a dedicated local reviewer session\n(`local/bin/review.sh`, dispatched after green local CI; a session never\nreviews its own diff) against these criteria:\n\n1. **Proof correctness** — No unexplained `sorry`. No `axiom` unless discussed.\n2. **Mathlib style** — Follow the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_doc` references.\n3. **Paper terminology** — Public Lean names and documentation should use\n   terminology from the paper and blueprint. See `docs/mathematical_language.md`.\n4. **Linter hygiene** — Fix warnings, don't mask them with broad\n   `set_option linter.<name> false` blocks.\n5. **Type safety** — No universe mismatches, coercion problems.\n6. **Performance** — Avoid expensive tactics on large types.\n7. **Modularity** — Are new lemmas general enough to be reused?\n8. **Documentation** — Every new `def` and major `theorem` must have a docstring.\n9. **Blueprint sync and paper origin** — Add `\\lean{}` and `\\leanok` tags for\n   formalized statements only when the Lean statement matches the source.\n   Record formalization-only auxiliary lemmas explicitly.\n10. **Scaffolding integrity** — Verify scaffolding aligns with Mathlib.\n11. **Statement drift** — Compare source-labelled theorem statements with the\n   paper and flag new hypotheses, weakened conclusions, changed quantifier\n   order, altered error parameters, or bridge/residual packages moving toward\n   a paper theorem.\n12. **Proof-evasion anti-patterns** — Review against `docs/anti_patterns.md`.\n\nFor full details, see `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` and the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_pr-review` reference.\n\n## Blueprint and Documentation Work\n\nIf modifying blueprint material:\n\n- Keep chapter structure under `blueprint/src/chapter/`\n- Ensure `leanblueprint web` succeeds\n- Keep Lean declaration references valid\n- Sync theorem labels with Lean names\n- Add `\\lean{LeanDeclName}` and `\\leanok` tags for formalized statements\n\nFor blueprint style conventions, see `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md`.\n\nFor temporary conditional scaffolding and the `\\lean{}`/`\\leanok` tagging\nstrategy, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n## Agent Rule Sources\n\nChecked in this repository snapshot:\n\n- No `.cursorrules`\n- No `.cursor/rules/`\n- No `.github/copilot-instructions.md`\n\n### Skills\n\nThe `texra-lean-skills` plugin (texra-ai/texra-lean-skills) carries the\ncanonical Mathlib-style, proof-integrity, and prose convention texts as the\n`lean-conventions` skill. Claude Code installs it automatically via\n`.claude/settings.json`; other agents install it by cloning the\nrepository and symlinking the skill directories into their skill\nlocation, as described in its README.\nMIPStarRE-local addenda to those conventions live in\n`docs/project_conventions.md`, which restates no shared rule.\n\nUse this file together with:\n\n| File | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| `CLAUDE.md` | Claude Code-specific notes (minimal pointer to this file) |\n| `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` | PR format, issue templates, label taxonomy, review checklist |\n| `lean-conventions` skill | Mathlib style, naming, documentation, PR review, proof integrity, prose style (canonical; installed) |\n| `docs/project_conventions.md` | MIPStarRE-local addenda to the shared conventions |\n| `docs/anti_patterns.md` | Subtler proof-evasion patterns |\n| `docs/proof_frontier_review.md` | Review checklist for construction theorems and residual inputs |\n| `docs/mathematical_language.md` | Project-local terminology rules |\n| `docs/blueprint_style_guide.md` | Blueprint notation and section conventions |\n| `docs/api_surface.md` | Useful obligation-closing lemmas for `SubMeas` |\n| `docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex` | Paper-gap documentation conventions |\n| `docs/paper-gaps/proof-gap-protocol.tex` | Protocol distinguishing source theorems, proof obligations, and conditional helpers |\n| `docs/formalization-patterns.md` | Conditional scaffolding, blueprint sync, split imports, and bridge records |\n| `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md` | Pedagogical notes on Mathlib and external lemmas |\n| `docs/ci-automation.md` | GitHub-era CI/CD reference (inactive; see `local/`) |\n| `docs/pr_review_management.md` | GitHub-era review-bot reference (lessons still apply; mechanism replaced by `local/protocols/review.md`) |\n| `local/DESIGN.md` | Local operations architecture and invariants |\n| `local/protocols/` | Normative protocols (meta, build cache, CI, review, auto-fix, issues/PRs, sessions) |\n| `local/personas/` | System prompts for locally dispatched agent roles |\n| `audits/` | Chapter-by-chapter scouting reports |\n| Pinned memories (external agent tooling) | Agent session memory maintained by the agent runtime; not a directory in the repository checkout. Pinned memories contain accumulated project lessons |\n\n## Local Operations\n\nThis repository runs its whole workflow locally. The short version every\nagent must know:\n\n- **Build reuse.** A hot main cache lives under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`;\n  fresh worktrees get it via `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` (which also\n  installs git hooks and resets dirty vendored packages). Never run\n  `lake update`; never write to the cache; at most one full `lake build`\n  runs machine-wide (the scripts take the lock for you).\n- **Lifecycle.** GitHub issue → branch `issue-<number>-slug` + worktree →\n  agent sessions → `local/bin/ci.sh` → `local/bin/review.sh` → optional\n  `local/bin/autofix.sh` → `local/bin/pr_merge.py`. CI and review evidence are\n  exact-head commit statuses (`local-ci/*`, `local-review/summary`); merges go\n  through GitHub with an exact-SHA guard. Details: `local/README.md`,\n  `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`.\n- **Sessions.** Dispatch, resume, and archive agent sessions only via\n  `local/bin/dispatch.sh` (roles: orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier,\n  blueprint, splitter, scout) so token/time telemetry stays complete.\n- **Telemetry duty.** Incidents go to `results/telemetry/events.md`;\n  protocol changes follow `local/protocols/meta.md` and are ledgered in\n  `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md`.\n- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s automated commits are prefixed\n  `[codex-auto-fix]` / `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review skip keys on\n  them); operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(review): …` /\n  `fix(ci): …` subjects so they are reviewed. Issue titles, slugs, and branch\n  names stay bracket-free.\n\n## Practical Defaults for Agents\n\nWhen editing Lean code:\n\n1. Read the paper source\n2. Read the target Lean file and nearby supporting files\n3. Type-check the single file\n4. Scan for `sorry|axiom`\n5. Run `lake build` only when the local change is stable\n\nWhen editing blueprint files:\n\n1. Read the matching paper source and chapter file\n2. Update Lean links carefully\n3. Run `leanblueprint web`\n\nPrefer minimal, dependency-aware changes that preserve the project's theorem\nstructure.\n\n</INSTRUCTIONS>"},{"type":"input_text","text":"<environment_context>\n  <cwd>/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0035-ch12-locators</cwd>\n  <shell>bash</shell>\n  <current_date>2026-09-04</current_date>\n  <timezone>Asia/Shanghai</timezone>\n  <filesystem><workspace_roots><root>/home/drx/MIPStarRE-qpbt/.worktrees/issue-0035-ch12-locators</root></workspace_roots><permission_profile type=\"managed\"><file_system type=\"restricted\"><entry access=\"read\"><special>:root</special></entry></file_system></permission_profile></filesystem>\n</environment_context>"}],"internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough":{"turn_id":"01a0683b-633b-7801-8479-aba0a0359b66","create_time":1788455117.6841025,"content_item_kinds":["agents_md.instructions","environments.environment_context"]}}}

This is the **single\nsource of truth** for agent conventions. Claude Code agents should also read\n`CLAUDE.md` for Claude-specific notes.\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository is a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization project for mathematics\naround $MIP^* = RE$. It is the **local-only continuation** of\n[LionSR/MIPStarRE](https://github.com/LionSR/MIPStarRE): the inherited track is\nthe **low individual degree test (LDT)** paper (arXiv:2009.12982); the active\ntrack is the **quantum Pauli basis test (QPBT)** from *MIP\\*=RE*\n(arXiv:2001.04383, primary) and *NEEXP in MIP\\** (arXiv:1904.05870, secondary).\n\nCI, review, and auto-fix **execute locally**; issues, PRs, their evidence and\nmerges live on GitHub (`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`), reached only through\n`local/bin/gh_common.py`. Read `local/README.md` and `local/DESIGN.md` before\ndoing workflow actions; the `## Local Operations` section below summarizes the\nrules.\n\nKey locations:\n\n- `references/qpbt-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of MIP\\*=RE\n  (arXiv:2001.04383); the QPBT lives in\n  `08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex` and\n  `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`\n- `references/neexp-paper/` — per-section TeX mirror of NEEXP in MIP\\*\n  (arXiv:1904.05870); secondary source\n  (`07_a_self_test_for_the_pauli_basis.tex`)\n- `references/ldt-paper/` — in-repo TeX source mirror for LDT\n- `blueprint/src/` — active LaTeX blueprint with Lean cross-references\n  (`\\lean{}`, `\\leanok`)\n- `MIPStarRE/` — Lean codebase matching the blueprint\n- `audits/` — dated audit reports, scouting notes, and repair plans\n- `local/`, `results/telemetry/` — the local workflow layer\n\nA legacy 2111 tensor track exists under `blueprint/legacy/` — do not modify it.\n\n**Canonical source hierarchy** (use in this order):\n\n1. `references/` paper mirrors — TeX source of the papers\n2. `blueprint/src/chapter/` — active LaTeX blueprint\n3. `MIPStarRE/` — Lean scaffold\n\nAlways read the paper source before formalizing or proving a statement. The\npaper contains the precise mathematical definitions, theorem statements, and\nproof strategies that the Lean code must faithfully represent. When stuck on a\nsorry site or proof, go back to the original paper TeX source — the answer is\nalmost always there. Do not guess or try random tactics without first\nunderstanding the paper's proof strategy.\n\n## Repository Layout\n\n```\nMIPStarRE/\n├── Quantum/               # Reusable matrix / measurement infrastructure\n│   ├── FiniteMatrix.lean  # Op d, normalizedTrace, tauNormSq, IsProj, ...\n│   └── Measurement.lean   # POVM, measurement types\n└── LDT/                   # Low individual degree test (13 submodules)\n    ├── Basic/             # Parameters, operators, distributions, submeasurements\n    ├── Test/              # Test definitions & main theorem\n    ├── Preliminaries/\n    ├── MakingMeasurementsProjective/\n    ├── MainInductionStep/\n    ├── ExpansionHypercubeGraph/\n    ├── GlobalVariance/\n    ├── SelfImprovement/\n    ├── CommutativityPoints/\n    ├── Commutativity/\n    └── Pasting/\n```\n\nEach LDT submodule typically has `Defs.lean` and `Theorems.lean`. Root imports\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\n\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\n\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\n\n### First-time setup\n\n```bash\nlake exe cache get\nlake build\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\n```\n\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR.  The hooks\nmove fast statement-integrity, proof-debt, changed-file Lean, and blueprint-sync\nchecks to the local workflow so CI is not spent on preventable statement drift.\n\n### Full project build (CI-equivalent)\n\n```bash\nlake build\n```\n\n### Fast single-file type-check (default iteration loop)\n\n```bash\nlake env lean MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in one file\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE/LDT/SelfImprovement/Defs.lean || true\n```\n\n### Check for proof holes in the whole project\n\n```bash\nrg -n \"sorry|axiom\" MIPStarRE\n```\n\n### Declaration checker\n\n```bash\nlake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls\n```\n\nUse this when blueprint declaration lists need to match Lean declarations.\n\n### Blueprint build\n\n```bash\nleanblueprint pdf    # PDF output\nleanblueprint web    # HTML output (use as default for quick checks)\n```\n\nIn CI, blueprint linting effectively runs `leanblueprint web` from `blueprint/`.\n\n### What counts as a single test\n\nThis repository does not have a conventional unit-test suite. The closest\nsingle-test commands are:\n\n- **Lean work**: `lake env lean path/to/File.lean` and\n  `rg -n \"sorry|axiom\" path/to/File.lean || true`\n- **Blueprint work**: `leanblueprint web`\n- **Whole-repo verification**: `lake build` and\n  `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n### Recommended validation sequence\n\nFor a Lean file change:\n\n1. Type-check the edited file with `lake env lean ...`\n2. Scan that file for `sorry|axiom`\n3. If the change affects imports or shared declarations, run `lake build`\n\nFor blueprint changes:\n\n1. Run `leanblueprint web`\n2. If declaration links changed, run `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls`\n\n## Toolchain\n\n- **Lean**: v4.31.0 (from `lean-toolchain`)\n- **Mathlib**: v4.31.0 (from `lakefile.toml`)\n\nImportant `lakefile.toml` options:\n\n- `relaxedAutoImplicit = false` — declare all variables explicitly\n- `pp.unicode.fun = true`\n- `weak.linter.mathlibStandardSet = true`\n- `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`\n\n## Proof-Filling Order\n\nSections must be filled in this dependency order:\n\n1. Sections 3–4: test setup and preliminaries\n2. Section 5: making measurements projective\n3. Sections 7–8: expansion and global variance\n4. Section 9: self-improvement\n5. Sections 10–11: commutativity\n6. Section 12: pasting\n7. Section 6: main induction wrapper\n\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\n\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\n\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\nthe paper theorem.\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\n\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\leanok` only\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\n\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\n\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\nfrom the blueprint by `\\lean{...}` and `\\leanok`.\n\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\n`prop:*`):\n\n1. Read the corresponding statement in `references/ldt-paper/`.\n2. Preserve the public Lean theorem statement, except for hypotheses that are\n   genuinely part of the faithful encoding of the paper's domain.\n3. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\n6. Do not point a source-labelled blueprint theorem to the conditional helper\n   with `\\leanok`.\n\nWhen reviewing an existing bridge, residual, repair, producer, or package\nhypothesis, first try to recover any genuine proof content from its construction\nand turn that content into a source-faithful lemma.  If the bridge does not\nactually follow from the paper hypotheses, do not preserve the paper theorem as\na strengthened statement.  Restore the paper-aligned theorem statement and leave\nthe missing proof obligation explicit, even if that means reintroducing a\ntracked `sorry` during a repair PR.\n\nSome side conditions are not deviations: positivity needed to define a\ndivision, nonemptiness of a finite type, decidability instances, field-model\ninstances, and similar boundary hypotheses may be faithful encodings of\nassumptions that the paper leaves implicit.  These should still be reviewed and\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\n\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\n`\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\n\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\nintegrity audit:\n\n- paper assumptions;\n- Lean assumptions;\n- paper conclusion;\n- Lean conclusion;\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\n\n### Paper-realignment mode\n\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\n\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\n\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\n\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\n\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\n\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\nhypotheses.\n\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\nminimal form is:\n\n```text\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.LowDegreeCode

/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code

This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
  | false => 0
  | true => 1

/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)

/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (y z : Cube m) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
  simp_rw [hfactor]
  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]

/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]

/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0

/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g

/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]

end MIPStarRE.QPBT
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.Polynomials

/-!
# The low-degree encoding

This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.

## References

The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
-/

open scoped BigOperators
open MvPolynomial

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
-/
abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool

/--
The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
-/
noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)

/--
The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
-/
noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y

/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
-/
noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)

/--
The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
-/
noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)

/--
The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
-/
theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
  | false => 0
  | true => 1

/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)

/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0

/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g

/-- The full-field specialization of `decodeAt` used by the generic algebra
layer.  The Chapter 16 `Poly`-facing name is defined in `Algebra/Decoding.lean`.
Every value is retained because the filter is `H = Finset.univ`, so this is the
cube-indexed evaluation of a polynomial representative.  The restricted
decoder identity remains separate and is only available for encoding
representatives; no unrestricted interpolation identity is asserted here.

This is the `H = \F_q` reading of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, used by Chapter 16 at
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex:11-20`; paper origin
`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1419-1420` and
the correction recorded in `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex`. -/
noncomputable def decodeFqRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Cube m → K :=
  decodeAt (Finset.univ : Finset K) (fun x => MvPolynomial.eval x g)

/-- A polynomial representative lies in the low-degree encoding image when it
is exactly the multilinear representative reconstructed from its full-field
decoder.  This predicate is used to state the support restriction required by
the Chapter 16 decoding argument; it does not identify arbitrary polynomial
functions with their representatives.

See `docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_decoding-identity.tex:87-116`. -/
def IsEncodingRep {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (g : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : Prop :=
  lowDegreeEncoding (decodeFqRep g) = g

`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
  sorry

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code

This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries

/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
  | false => 0
  | true => 1

/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)

/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (y z : Cube m) :
    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
  classical
  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
  simp_rw [hfactor]
  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]

/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]

/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0

/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g

/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
  funext y
  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]

end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# The low-degree encoding
     5	
     6	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials
     7	and packages the resulting low-degree code as honest polynomial representatives.
     8	
     9	## References
    10	
    11	The source-facing nodes are `def:polynomials-degree`,
    12	`def:low-degree-encoding`, and `def:indicator-vector` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:321-417`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    15	The polynomial class `def:polyfunc` is reused from
    16	`MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` (the LDT formalization).
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	open MvPolynomial
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	/- The Boolean cube indexes the `2^m` qudits in the low-degree encoding. -/
    25	/-- The Boolean cube indexing the `2^m` qudits of the test.  This is the index
    26	type in `def:low-degree-encoding`, blueprint
    27	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    28	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    29	-/
    30	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool
    31	
    32	/--
    33	The representative polynomial which is `1` at `y` on the Boolean cube and
    34	zero at the other cube points.  This is the indicator polynomial in
    35	`def:low-degree-encoding` (blueprint lines 381-401; paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).
    37	-/
    38	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    39	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    40	  ∏ i : Fin m, if y i then X i else (1 - X i)
    41	
    42	/--
    43	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    44	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    45	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`; paper origin:
    47	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    48	-/
    49	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    50	    (a : Cube m → K) : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=
    51	  ∑ y : Cube m, a y • indicatorPoly y
    52	
    53	/- Evaluation shorthand for the representative polynomial in
    54	`def:low-degree-encoding`; it is Lean-only notation. -/
    55	/-- Evaluation shorthand for the low-degree encoding.  Blueprint
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:381-401`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    60	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) : K :=
    61	  eval x (lowDegreeEncoding a)
    62	
    63	/--
    64	The indicator vector `ind_m(x)` of `def:indicator-vector`.
    65	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`; paper origin:
    66	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    67	-/
    68	noncomputable def indicatorVec {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (x : Fin m → K) : Cube m → K :=
    70	  fun y => eval x (indicatorPoly y)
    71	
    72	/--
    73	The defining dot-product identity for the encoding, corresponding to
    74	Equation `eq:low-degree-encoding-definition` and `def:indicator-vector` in the
    75	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:403-417`, paper origin
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.
    77	-/
    78	theorem lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
    79	    (a : Cube m → K) (x : Fin m → K) :
    80	    lowDegreeEnc a x = dotProduct a (indicatorVec x) := by
    81	  simp [lowDegreeEnc, lowDegreeEncoding, indicatorVec, dotProduct]
    82	
    83	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
     1	import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.LowDegreeCode
     2	
     3	/-! # Decoding maps for the low-degree code
     4	
     5	This file supplies `def:decoding-map` and the Boolean cube embedding from
     6	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
     7	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	open scoped BigOperators
    11	
    12	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    13	
    14	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries
    15	
    16	/-- The formalization-only embedding of Boolean coordinates into a field used by
    17	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    18	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    19	def boolToScalar {K : Type*} [Field K] : Bool → K
    20	  | false => 0
    21	  | true => 1
    22	
    23	/-- The coordinatewise Boolean-cube embedding used by
    24	`def:decoding-map`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper
    25	`04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    26	def cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ} : Cube m → (Fin m → K) :=
    27	  fun y i => boolToScalar (y i)
    28	
    29	/-- On the Boolean cube, an indicator polynomial evaluates to the corresponding
    30	Kronecker delta.  This is the interpolation observation at paper lines 880-891. -/
    31	private theorem eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    32	    (y z : Cube m) :
    33	    MvPolynomial.eval (cubeEmbed (K := K) z) (indicatorPoly (K := K) y) =
    34	      if y = z then 1 else 0 := by
    35	  classical
    36	  rw [indicatorPoly, MvPolynomial.eval_prod]
    37	  simp only [apply_ite, MvPolynomial.eval_X, MvPolynomial.eval_sub, map_one]
    38	  have hfactor (i : Fin m) :
    39	      (if y i then cubeEmbed (K := K) z i else 1 - cubeEmbed (K := K) z i) =
    40	        if y i = z i then 1 else 0 := by
    41	    cases hy : y i <;> cases hz : z i <;> simp_all [cubeEmbed, boolToScalar]
    42	  simp_rw [hfactor]
    43	  rw [Fintype.prod_boole]
    44	  split_ifs <;> simp_all [funext_iff]
    45	
    46	/-- Evaluating a low-degree encoding at an embedded Boolean point recovers its
    47	coefficient at that point, as stated at paper line 891. -/
    48	private theorem lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}
    49	    (a : Cube m → K) (z : Cube m) :
    50	    lowDegreeEnc a (cubeEmbed z) = a z := by
    51	  rw [lowDegreeEnc_eq_dotProduct]
    52	  simp [dotProduct, indicatorVec, eval_indicatorPoly_cubeEmbed]
    53	
    54	/-- The decoding map `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    55	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    56	noncomputable def decodeAt {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    57	    (H : Finset K) (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    58	  fun y => if g (cubeEmbed y) ∈ H then g (cubeEmbed y) else 0
    59	
    60	/-- Boolean specialization of `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    61	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    62	noncomputable abbrev decodeBool {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    63	    (g : (Fin m → K) → K) : Cube m → K :=
    64	  decodeAt ({0, 1} : Finset K) g
    65	
    66	/-- The restricted decoding identity in `def:decoding-map`, blueprint
    67	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:445-455`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:917-924`. -/
    68	theorem decodeAt_lowDegreeEnc {K : Type*} [Field K] [DecidableEq K] {m : ℕ}
    69	    (H : Finset K) (a : Cube m → K) (ha : ∀ y, a y ∈ H) :
    70	    decodeAt H (lowDegreeEnc a) = a := by
    71	  funext y
    72	  simp [decodeAt, lowDegreeEnc_cubeEmbed, ha y]
    73	
    74	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-!
     6	# Polynomial preliminaries
     7	
     8	Packages the paper's low-individual-degree polynomial class together
     9	with Schwartz-Zippel bounds as thin wrappers around Mathlib's existing
    10	multivariate polynomial theorems.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	* `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex`, Section 3 (Preliminaries)

    16	
    17	open Finset Fintype
    18

    25	/-- `\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}` from the paper's definition of low-individual-degree
    26	polynomials. This is Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.restrictDegree` submodule. -/
    27	noncomputable abbrev polyFunc (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [CommSemiring K] (d : ℕ) :
    28	    Submodule K (MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) :=
    29	  MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin m) K d
    30	
    31	/-- If `p ∈ polyFunc m K d`, then `p.degreeOf i ≤ d` for every variable `i`. -/
    32	theorem degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    33	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hp : p ∈ polyFunc m K d) (i : Fin m) :
    34	    p.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
    35	  MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mpr fun s hs =>
    36	    (MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree (σ := Fin m) (R := K) p d).mp hp s hs i
    37	
    38	/-- Paper label `rem:individual-degree-convention`.
    39	
    40	Increasing the individual-degree bound enlarges the corresponding low-degree
    41	polynomial class. -/
    42	theorem polyFuncMonotone {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K] :
    43	    polyFunc m K d ≤ polyFunc m K (d + 1) := by
    44	  intro p hp
    45	  rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree] at hp ⊢
    46	  intro s hs i
    47	  exact (hp s hs i).trans (Nat.le_succ d)
    48	
    49	/-- The uniform agreement probability of two polynomials on `K^m`, written as a
    50	finite cardinality ratio over `K^m`. -/
    51	noncomputable def polynomialAgreementProbability (m : ℕ) (K : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype K]
    52	    [DecidableEq K] (g h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K) : ℚ≥0 :=
    53	  #{x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    54	      MvPolynomial.eval x g = MvPolynomial.eval x h} /
    55	    (Fintype.card K ^ m : ℚ≥0)
    56	
    57	/-- If every individual degree of `p` is at most `d`, then the total degree of
    58	`p` is at most `m * d`. -/
    59	theorem totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [CommSemiring K]
    60	    {p : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hdeg : ∀ i, p.degreeOf i ≤ d) :
    61	    p.totalDegree ≤ m * d := by
    62	  rw [MvPolynomial.totalDegree]
    63	  refine Finset.sup_le ?_
    64	  intro s hs
    65	  calc
    66	    s.sum (fun _ e => e) = ∑ i : Fin m, s i := by
    67	      rw [Finsupp.sum_fintype]
    68	      intro i
    69	      rfl
    70	    _ ≤ ∑ _i : Fin m, d := by
    71	      refine Finset.sum_le_sum ?_
    72	      intro i _
    73	      exact (MvPolynomial.degreeOf_le_iff.mp (hdeg i)) s hs
    74	    _ = m * d := by
    75	      simp [Fintype.card_fin]
    76	
    77	/-- If two polynomials on `K^m` have total degree at most `d`, then the uniform
    78	agreement probability is at most `d / |K|`. -/
    79	theorem schwartzZippel_totalDegree {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
    80	    [DecidableEq K] {g h : MvPolynomial (Fin m) K} (hneq : g ≠ h)
    81	    (hg : g.totalDegree ≤ d) (hh : h.totalDegree ≤ d) :
    82	    polynomialAgreementProbability m K g h ≤ d / Fintype.card K := by
    83	  have hsub_ne : g - h ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hneq
    84	  have hsub_deg : (g - h).totalDegree ≤ d :=
    85	    (MvPolynomial.totalDegree_sub g h).trans (max_le hg hh)
    86	  unfold polynomialAgreementProbability
    87	  rw [show {x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    88	        MvPolynomial.eval x g = MvPolynomial.eval x h} =
    89	      {x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    90	        MvPolynomial.eval x (g - h) = 0} by
    91	        ext x
    92	        simp [MvPolynomial.eval_sub, sub_eq_zero]]
    93	  calc
    94	    #{x ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m → K)) |
    95	        MvPolynomial.eval x (g - h) = 0} /
    96	        (Fintype.card K ^ m : ℚ≥0)
    97	      ≤ (g - h).totalDegree / Fintype.card K := by
    98	          simpa using
    99	            (MvPolynomial.schwartz_zippel_totalDegree
   100	              (n := m) (p := g - h) hsub_ne (Finset.univ : Finset K))
   101	    _ ≤ d / Fintype.card K := by
   102	          gcongr
   103	
   104	/-- Schwartz-Zippel for the paper's low-individual-degree class
   105	`\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}`. -/
   106	theorem schwartzZippel_individualDegree {m d : ℕ} {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K]
   107	    [DecidableEq K] (g h : polyFunc m K d) (hneq : g ≠ h) :
   108	    polynomialAgreementProbability m K g.1 h.1 ≤ ((m * d : ℕ) : ℚ≥0) / Fintype.card K := by
   109	  have hval_ne : g.1 ≠ h.1 := by
   110	    intro hgh
   111	    apply hneq
   112	    exact Subtype.ext hgh
   113	  have hg_degOf : ∀ i, g.1.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
   114	    degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc g.property
   115	  have hh_degOf : ∀ i, h.1.degreeOf i ≤ d :=
   116	    degreeOf_le_of_mem_polyFunc h.property
   117	  exact schwartzZippel_totalDegree (g := g.1) (h := h.1) hval_ne
   118	    (totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le hg_degOf)
   119	    (totalDegree_le_mul_of_degreeOf_le hh_degOf)

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file records that choice as
     8	data, while exposing Mathlib's basis and algebra-trace APIs for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The declarations correspond to `def:admissible-size`, `def:subfields-kappa`,
    13	`def:subfield-trace`, and `def:binary-representation` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-232` and `298-315`.
    15	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    23	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    24	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    25	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    26	-/
    27	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    28	
    29	/--
    30	A fixed finite-field model records the carrier and the chosen coding of its
    31	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
    32	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
    33	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
    34	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.
    37	-/
    38	/- The finite-field carrier is specialized to `Type 0`, as are the finite
    39	models used by the surrounding Euclidean-space API. -/
    40	structure FixedFieldModel (q : ℕ) extends MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel.{0} q where
    41	  /-- Scalar restriction from `ZMod 2` to the chosen field. -/
    42	  algebra : Algebra (ZMod 2) K
    43	  /-- Dimension of the chosen basis over the prime subfield. -/
    44	  basisDim : ℕ
    45	  /-- The chosen basis dimension is odd, as required for a self-dual normal basis
    46	  over the binary field. -/
    47	  basisDimOdd : Odd basisDim
    48	  /-- The admissible field-size relation for the chosen basis dimension. -/
    49	  basisCard : q = 2 ^ basisDim
    50	  /-- The chosen basis of `K` over `ZMod 2`. -/
    51	  basis : Module.Basis (Fin basisDim) (ZMod 2) K
    52	  /--
    53	  The inherited coding of `K` is the natural binary encoding of the stored
    54	  basis coordinates.  This field records the source's `downsize` convention
    55	  rather than allowing an unrelated permutation of `Fin q`.  It is the
    56	  coordinate clause of `def:binary-representation` in
    57	  `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, with paper origin
    58	  `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:669-680`.
    59	  -/
    60	  representation_natural :
    61	    ∀ v : Fin basisDim → ZMod 2,
    62	      (toFieldModel.equiv (basis.equivFun.symm v)).val =
    63	        ∑ i : Fin basisDim, if v i = 1 then 2 ^ i.1 else 0
    64	  /-- Self-duality of the chosen basis with respect to the field trace. -/
    65	  selfDual : ∀ i j, Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (basis i * basis j) =
    66	    if i = j then 1 else 0
    67	  /-- Normality of the chosen basis, recorded by a Frobenius generator. -/
    68	  normal : ∃ α : K, ∀ i, basis i = α ^ (2 ^ i.1)

    31	elements by `Fin q`.  The algebra structure and stored basis data make explicit
    32	the paper's once-and-for-all self-dual normal-basis convention; they are
    33	deliberately part of the model rather than quantified afresh by the soundness
    34	theorem.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:binary-representation`, blueprint
    35	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`, paper origin
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-728`.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: scripts/install_git_hooks.sh [--install|--check|--help]

Install or verify the repository-local Git hooks for the current worktree.

  --install  Set core.hooksPath to .githooks. This is the default.
  --check    Verify that core.hooksPath points to .githooks and hooks are executable.
  --help     Show this help text.
EOF
}

MODE="install"
case "${1:-}" in
  ""|--install)
    MODE="install"
    ;;
  --check|--verify)
    MODE="check"
    ;;
  --help|-h)
    usage
    exit 0
    ;;
  *)
    usage >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
cd "$ROOT"

if [ ! -d .githooks ]; then
  echo "No .githooks directory found at repository root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

check_hook_files() {
  HOOK_STATUS=0
  for HOOK in .githooks/pre-commit .githooks/pre-push
  do
    if [ ! -f "$HOOK" ]; then
      echo "Missing hook file: $HOOK" >&2
      HOOK_STATUS=1
    elif [ ! -x "$HOOK" ]; then
      echo "Hook file is not executable: $HOOK" >&2
      HOOK_STATUS=1
    fi
  done
  return "$HOOK_STATUS"
}

check_hooks_installed() {
  INSTALL_STATUS=0
  CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH="$(git config --get core.hooksPath || true)"
  case "$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH" in
    .githooks|"$ROOT/.githooks")
      ;;
    "")
      echo "core.hooksPath is not set for this worktree." >&2
      INSTALL_STATUS=1
      ;;
    *)
      echo "core.hooksPath is '$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH', not .githooks." >&2
      INSTALL_STATUS=1
      ;;
  esac

  if ! check_hook_files; then
    INSTALL_STATUS=1
  fi

  if [ "$INSTALL_STATUS" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "MIPStarRE Git hooks are installed for this worktree."
    echo "core.hooksPath=$CURRENT_HOOKS_PATH"
  else
    echo "Run scripts/install_git_hooks.sh to install the repository hooks." >&2
  fi
  return "$INSTALL_STATUS"
}

if [ "$MODE" = "check" ]; then
  check_hooks_installed
  exit $?
fi
